{"body":"## Problem

The active governance rule set is inconsistent across the public/bootstrap sources.

From the site/repo review:

- `bootstrap.json` appears to list active rules only through `gov-09-agent-continuity-bootstrap`.
- `agent.txt` also refers to GOV-01 through GOV-09 as the active set.
- The published governance documentation/sidebar includes GOV-01 through GOV-13.
- Release history indicates GOV-10 through GOV-13 exist as harness-engineering governance rules.

This creates ambiguity for agents and users: should GOV-10 to GOV-13 be installed, ignored, treated as preview, or treated as optional extensions?

Because VibeGov is itself a governance source of truth, this mismatch undermines trust in the bootstrap contract.

## Affected areas

Likely affected files/outputs:

- `static/bootstrap.json`
- `static/agent.txt`
- `docs/bootstrap` / bootstrap contract docs
- published governance docs/sidebar
- any bootstrap validation assumptions
- release notes or rule index pages if they describe the active set

## Recommended fix

Decide one clear rule-set status:

### Preferred option

Make GOV-01 through GOV-13 the active published rule set everywhere.

Update active rule references to include:

- `gov-10-agent-state-closure-git-hygiene`
- `gov-11-agent-legibility-in-repo-truth`
- `gov-12-drift-control-garbage-collection`
- `gov-13-review-loops-completion-discipline`

### Alternative option

If GOV-10 to GOV-13 are not intended to be core yet, clearly label them as one of:

- extended rules
- preview rules
- optional harness rules
- experimental rules

Then make the docs/sidebar reflect that status.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bootstrap.json` and `agent.txt` agree on the active rule set.
- [ ] Bootstrap docs use the same rule range/status as the machine-readable sources.
- [ ] Published docs/sidebar clearly distinguish active vs optional/preview rules if applicable.
- [ ] A new user or agent can determine exactly which rules should be installed during bootstrap.
- [ ] No public page implies GOV-10 to GOV-13 are active while machine-readable sources omit them, or vice versa.

## Priority
